# Josupeit.Practices.Commands

> Abstract base classes for the CQRS contracts in `Josupeit.Practices.Commands.Abstractions`: `Command`, `Command<TInput>`, `CommandWithOutput<TOutput>`, `CommandWithOutput<TInput, TOutput>`, `Query<TOutput>`, and `Query<TInput, TOutput>`. Override either the synchronous `Execute` or the asynchronous `ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken)` and the other direction is bridged automatically; calling the base implementation from an override, or overriding neither, is detected at run time and reported as an `InvalidOperationException` instead of a stack overflow. Targets netstandard2.0 and net8.0, depends only on the Abstractions package, and lives in the `Josupeit.Practices.Commands` namespace.

Install with `dotnet add package Josupeit.Practices.Commands`; the Abstractions package comes along transitively. All types live in the `Josupeit.Practices.Commands` namespace, the same one as the interfaces. The package contains `Executable` (root class, not for direct use) and six abstract base classes:

- `Command` implements `ICommand` - no input, no output
- `Command<TInput>` implements `ICommand<TInput>` - one input, no output
- `CommandWithOutput<TOutput>` implements `ICommandWithOutput<TOutput>` - no input, returns `TOutput`
- `CommandWithOutput<TInput, TOutput>` implements `ICommandWithOutput<TInput, TOutput>` - one input, returns `TOutput`
- `Query<TOutput>` implements `IQuery<TOutput>` - no input, returns `TOutput`, must be pure
- `Query<TInput, TOutput>` implements `IQuery<TInput, TOutput>` - one input, returns `TOutput`, must be pure

Each base class has exactly two `virtual` override points - `Execute(...)` and `ExecuteAsync(..., CancellationToken)` - plus a non-virtual token-less `ExecuteAsync(...)` that funnels into the token-accepting overload. There are no abstract members: overriding nothing compiles and throws on first use. Never call `base.Execute` or `base.ExecuteAsync` from an override. The bridged synchronous path blocks with `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()` and cannot be canceled; the bridged asynchronous path runs synchronously and checks the token once up front. The recursion guard is scoped to the logical call chain (`AsyncLocal`), so one instance can serve concurrent callers and any DI lifetime works.

Unlike MediatR-style libraries, a command is the executable object itself - behavior plus injected collaborators - not a message dispatched to a separate handler; there is no `Send()` or `IRequestHandler`.

- [PublicAPI.Shipped.txt](https://codeberg.org/DerPeit/Josupeit.Practices/raw/branch/main/src/Josupeit.Practices.Commands/PublicAPI.Shipped.txt): analyzer-enforced inventory of every public member. `!` marks non-nullable and `?` nullable reference types; the `virtual` prefix marks the override points; accessibility is not shown.
